title: Hazel and the Compass
premise: In 1848, on the eve of revolution in a Rhineland printing town, Petra Voss works her late father's type cases and keeps her head down — until the army requisitions the town and seizes the guild ledger holding every name of the men marked for conscription and punishment, including her brother's. Armed with a hidden brass compass that once belonged to a smuggled-out reformer, Petra joins a clandestine network of printers, widows, and a sympathetic clerk to reconstruct the ledger from memory, proofs, and buried archives before the victors' historians can burn the record. The race ends at the customs house, where Petra trades the compass for passage of the reconstructed ledger to Frankfurt, saving the names if not the town.
about_author: Paloma Underhill is the pen name of a former letterpress apprentice who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century print-shop equipment in small German towns. She writes historical fiction about ordinary people who keep records when power would prefer they didn't.

chapters.title: The Smell of Ink
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Introduces the Voss print shop, her father's recent death, and her quiet mastery of type cutting. Her brother Anton argues politics over dinner; she refuses to listen. Emotional beat: the comfort of routine on the edge of rupture.

chapters.title: Names in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. She discovers the guild ledger lists Anton among men flagged for conscription lists and old debts of dissent. She says nothing to him. Emotional beat: dread disguised as diligence.

chapters.title: Drums at the Bridge
chapters.summary: Anton's POV. Revolutionary crowds seize the bridge; the army answers with requisition orders. Anton is swept into organizing while Petra watches from the shop window. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Soldiers occupy the town square and confiscate the guild ledger as 'evidence.' The clerk Herr Brandt signs the receipt with shaking hands. Emotional beat: helplessness made bureaucratic.

chapters.title: The Brass Compass
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Among her father's effects she finds a compass engraved with a name she doesn't recognize and a note pointing to the cellar. Emotional beat: inheritance as mystery rather than comfort.

chapters.title: The Widow Kessler
chapters.summary: Widow Kessler's POV. The widow reveals the compass belonged to a printer smuggled out after the last crackdown, and that her husband died hiding proof sheets. She asks Petra what she intends to do. Emotional beat: grief offered as instruction.

chapters.title: What the Army Burns First
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Smoke rises from the chancery annex; the army begins destroying 'seditious papers.' Petra realizes the ledger's names will not survive the occupation. Emotional beat: the moment passivity dies.

chapters.title: Proof Sheets in the Cellar
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. The clerk, guilt-ridden, brings Petra misprinted proof sheets containing fragments of the ledger. Together they begin reconstruction by lamplight. Emotional beat: complicity transformed into courage.

chapters.title: A Network of Small Hands
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided: apprentices carry messages in ink-stained sleeves, the widow shelters copies, a baker memorizes columns. Petra coordinates. Emotional beat: belonging found in conspiracy.

chapters.title: The Compass Points East
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Deciphering her father's note, she learns the compass hides a route map to a courier line running to Frankfurt's free presses. Emotional beat: awe at her father's hidden life.

chapters.title: Anton Taken
chapters.summary: Anton's POV. Arrested at a meeting, Anton is held with other named men pending transport. His chapter ends mid-interrogation. Emotional beat: terror without melodrama.

chapters.title: Bargaining with Brandt
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. Petra pressures the clerk to delay the transport manifest using his own requisition paperwork against it. He agrees, knowing it may hang him. Emotional beat: moral risk accepted.

chapters.title: The Informer
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A copy goes missing; suspicion falls on the baker's son. Petra must decide whether to confront or protect him. Emotional beat: paranoia testing trust.

chapters.title: Confession at the Mill
chapters.summary: The baker's son's POV. He confesses he copied pages to buy his father's safety, but kept the originals hidden. Petra forgives what she cannot forget. Emotional beat: mercy under pressure.

chapters.title: Reconstructing the Dead
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The network completes the ledger from memory, proofs, parish records, and the widow's letters. Petra sets the names in type herself. Emotional beat: mourning turned into craft.

chapters.title: The Victor's Historian
chapters.summary: Historian Dr. Falk's POV. A commission arrives to write the official account; Falk burns archives efficiently and interviews Petra, suspecting nothing — almost. Emotional beat: chilling civility.

chapters.title: Transport Night
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. The prisoners are moved up two days early; Brandt falsifies the manifest at gunpoint of his own conscience. Anton slips a note to Petra through a guard's glove. Emotional beat: desperation sharpened to precision.

chapters.title: The Customs House
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The courier line is compromised; the only way out is the customs house where Falk's commission stores sealed evidence. Petra offers the compass — the historian's coveted provenance piece — as a bribe for one unwatched hour. Emotional beat: sacrifice of the last link to her father.

chapters.title: Setting the Record
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Inside, she prints forty copies of the reconstructed ledger on the customs house's own press while Falk admires his new compass upstairs. Emotional beat: triumph rendered in the rhythm of the press.

chapters.title: What Fire Cannot Read
chapters.summary: Falk's POV. Discovering the theft, Falk burns the shop — but the copies are already sewn into grain sacks heading downriver. He writes his official history anyway, knowing it is now a lie with rivals. Emotional beat: victory hollowed out.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The town counts its losses; Anton returns transported but alive, having seen his own name in print in Frankfurt. Petra reopens the shop under the widow's sign. Emotional beat: exhausted, earned hope.

chapters.title: Hazel and the Compass
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, years later. Teaching an apprentice named Hazel, she explains the compass's true function was never navigation but memory — a pointer toward what must be kept. The final copy of the ledger rests openly on the shelf. Emotional beat: inheritance completed.
